items.name: BackPack
notes: Upstream documents reverse Iran-to-origin forwarding and direct layer-3 tunneling.
The installer downloads architecture-specific releases and verifies published SHA-256 checksums.
Tokens, setup links, panel credentials, recovery codes, API tokens, and backup archives are secrets.

items.name: WatTunnel
notes: Single Go binary wattun + wattun-manager; Kharej generates a wat1: token pasted into Iran; config at /etc/wattun/<name>.yml, unit wattun@<name>.service.

Installer verifies SHA256SUMS.sig with an embedded RSA key but runs the main branch as root unpinned, can silently skip verification (WAT_SKIP_CHECKSUM/missing openssl), and has unsigned paths (local dist, source build.sh, manager from raw main); service runs as root with setcap cap_net_raw/admin/bind_service.

Encrypts only the Iran<->Kharej leg - run an E2E protocol (VLESS+Reality/TLS/WireGuard) inside. The wat1: token contains the key and is a secret; never print or commit it. Vendor performance claims are unverified.

items.name: C-Tunnel
reverse_modes: frp+ (kernel L3/L2 over up to 8 parallel TLS-shaped TCP streams)
notes: Go binary + ctunnel-kernel helper + BackPack-style menu; manage menu derived from BackPack (AminMGMT). Config /etc/ctunnel/{state.json,panel.json,tunnels/<name>.env}; units ctunnel@<name> (kernel), ctunnel-engine@<name> (UDP-Crypt/EoIP/EtherIP), ctunnel-panel.

Installer verifies release SHA256SUMS and aborts on mismatch, but tracks main unpinned by default (pin v0.2.1) and the checksum ships with the binaries (integrity, not provenance); services run as root; web panel defaults to HTTP on a random path (keep off public internet).
UDP-Crypt sequence numbers are clock-based: both servers need NTP or UDP-Crypt methods silently break. Encrypts only the Iran<->Kharej leg - run an E2E protocol inside.

On Iran<->Kharej links, run `ctunnel conntest` first: international/native UDP (quic-v1, plain wireguard) is typically dropped while frp+ TCP streams and some UDP-Crypt (rudp-fec, wg-stealth) survive - verify per path. The ctunnel:// link carries keys and is a secret; never print or commit it. Vendor performance claims are unverified.
